facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Net leverage fell to 2.82x on last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 from 7.64x at year-end 2025, but the two ratios are not on one footing. At year-end 2025 consolidated debt, which also financed the businesses now held for sale, is set against the earnings of continuing operations alone. By 2026-09-30 the OEM sale proceeds had repaid the Term A-2 loan of USD 700.0 million and USD 490.0 million of the revolver. Holding EBITDA at the FY2025 level, net leverage at 2026-09-30 would still be 4.01x, so debt repayment explains most of the improvement and higher earnings the rest. The improvement for creditors rests mainly on sale proceeds applied to debt, not on a change in the earnings base. facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: The earnings improvement is real but includes items that do not recur. Last-twelve-months EBITDA includes a patent settlement gain of USD 25.0 million and a tariff refund benefit of USD 25.3 million, about 11.95% of that EBITDA; without them net leverage would be 3.21x, an Analyst Judgement shown in the register and not used in any fixed row. FY2025 earnings, by contrast, carry a non-cash asset impairment and a currency hedge gain, but both sit in FY2025 and in the nine months of 2025, so they cancel out of the last-twelve-months figure. The strongest contrary evidence is the rise in reported gross margin to 59.8% in nine months 2026 from 57.1%, which the issuer attributes mainly to lower VI Business inventory step-up charges and to the tariff refunds; the step-up fade is durable but the refunds are not, and a fourth quarter without one-off gains would settle how much of the improvement lasts. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C11

facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Cash generation improved but shareholder returns absorbed more than it. Last-twelve-months free cash flow after capital expenditure is positive and far above FY2025, which was close to zero after a build-up of receivables and higher tax payments, but it includes the patent settlement and tariff refunds in operating cash flow. In nine months 2026 cash paid for share repurchases was 3.08 times free cash flow, so the OEM sale proceeds also went to shareholders as well as to debt, and a further USD 41.4 million was repurchased after the quarter end. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Buyer power is high in government-funded markets. Hospitals buy through direct sales forces, representatives and distributors, most customer relationships outside the United States are with government entities, and governments use price controls, collective purchasing, competitive bidding and tenders, with China's volume-based procurement named as an adverse influence on future pricing; concentration among buyers is not disclosed. facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Political and regulatory factors work through tariffs and pricing rules. A court decision on 2026-02-20 invalidated the tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, replacement tariffs were imposed under other authority, and Teleflex received refunds that gave a USD 25.3 million benefit in continuing operations and USD 13.9 million in discontinued operations; more refund requests are expected in the fourth quarter with no receivable recorded, and the scope and durability of the replacement tariffs are uncertain. Gross margin and cash flow therefore carry tariff risk in both directions. Regulatory cost is shifting rather than rising: European Union Medical Device Regulation costs fell in the third quarter, the FDA quality system rule was replaced on 2026-02-02, and European Union certification is expected to complete in 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16

facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Economic factors work through currency, interest rates and energy. About 42.91% of nine-month revenue was earned outside North America, the principal currency exposures are the euro, Chinese renminbi, Mexican peso, Malaysian ringgit, Swiss franc and Canadian dollar, and Teleflex hedges with forward contracts of USD 547.3 million of notional and cross-currency swaps of USD 1.6 billion of notional at 2025-12-31, the swaps being designated as net investment hedges. A 10% rise in the dollar would raise the fair value of the hedge contracts by USD 179.5 million and a 10% fall would cut it by USD 182.2 million at that date. Floating-rate debt is 38.72% of principal, so a 1.0 percentage point rise in rates would add USD 6.32 million a year to interest cost, and the Middle East conflict is cited as a source of energy price and supply chain risk. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C09; calculation C13

facts.text: The main credit supports are cash generation, liquidity and maturity profile, not scale or diversification. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: Management has levers, and they are enough to avoid liquidity distress on the disclosed figures. It can suspend repurchases, since USD 400.0 million remains and the programme may be suspended at any time, hold the dividend, which costs about USD 53.94 million a year at the current share count and is 22.20% of last-twelve-months free cash flow, realise restructuring savings, and apply the Acute Care proceeds to the revolver. Free cash flow after dividends was USD 184.216 million over the last twelve months, so the realistic failure mode is slow leverage creep and loss of policy credibility, not default. The observable triggers are a revolver balance above USD 60.0 million at 2026-12-31, Interventional revenue and margin in the fourth quarter, any goodwill impairment charge, the pace of repurchases and the covenant disclosure in the next annual report. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C07

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Teleflex presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring single-use device demand, high Vascular and Surgical margins, low capital intensity and no note maturity before 2028-06-01, but credit quality is constrained by acquired rather than organic growth, a thin and impairment-sensitive Interventional segment, earnings that include USD 50.3 million of one-offs, shareholder payments of 2.53 times free cash flow and an unstated financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to 57.71% conversion of EBITDA into free cash flow and 3.47% capital intensity, tempered by working-capital timing and receipts that may not repeat. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding leverage near the current range through the fourth-quarter taxes, on the Acute Care proceeds, and on market access at roughly the 5.875% coupon paid in June 2026 as the 2028 notes approach in 2027, with no agency rating to anchor that access. The primary downside path is Interventional weakness and fading one-offs while the revolver funds taxes and repurchases, lifting leverage against covenants that cannot be checked. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector the profile is stronger on margin and free of a sponsor, and weaker on stated policy; the filings give no peer data, so that comparison is a judgement. The financial profile trend is better on leverage and cash flow but is not comparable across periods because the perimeter changed. Further analysis would require the covenant compliance calculation, letters of credit, the OEM tax amount, the proxy statement, the executed agreements, a leverage target and the securitization and Term A-1 terms. Analysis complete. Top risk: shareholder returns and tax payments absorbing the proceeds that reduced leverage. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C07; calculation C10; calculation C11

Source readiness for Teleflex Inc (issuer tfx-96943), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the five supplied SEC filings can support the requested Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit analyses, and which documents are missing.

No analysis from another module was supplied; this is the first module in the run. A retrieval record found beside the filings was not supplied as a source and is not used as evidence.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied Teleflex filings are enough to run the requested Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit analyses, but only on the continuing-operations perimeter and with named limits, so creditors should treat any liquidity or covenant headroom conclusion as provisional.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-K_2024-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 102

The September 2026 quarterly report controls current debt, debt terms and the pending sale of the Acute Care and Interventional Urology businesses. It does not state letters of credit, undrawn revolver capacity, reported covenant ratios or a debt maturity table, so those inputs stay open. The 2024 annual report covers the whole company before the divestitures and is comparable with later periods only through the recast figures in the 2025 annual report. No ratings, credit agreement, indenture, earnings release, peer or market data were supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 109

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net leverage on continuing operations fell to 2.82x at 2026-09-30 from 7.64x at year-end 2025, mostly because OEM sale proceeds repaid debt, and pending tax payments and the Acute Care sale will move net debt in both directions before the position settles.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C09

Teleflex states no EBITDA, so the figure is derived from reported statement lines; the last-twelve-months result includes one-off gains from a patent settlement and tariff refunds, without which net leverage would be 3.21x, and the year-end 2025 ratio divides consolidated debt by the earnings of continuing operations only. Interest cover on cash interest was 2.48x for FY2025 and cannot be updated for 2026 because nine-month cash interest is not stated. Letters of credit under the revolver at 2026-09-30 and a debt maturity table after the May 2026 refinancing are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 141; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C11

### Financial interpretation

Net leverage fell to 2.82x on last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 from 7.64x at year-end 2025, but the two ratios are not on one footing. At year-end 2025 consolidated debt, which also financed the businesses now held for sale, is set against the earnings of continuing operations alone. By 2026-09-30 the OEM sale proceeds had repaid the Term A-2 loan of USD 700.0 million and USD 490.0 million of the revolver. Holding EBITDA at the FY2025 level, net leverage at 2026-09-30 would still be 4.01x, so debt repayment explains most of the improvement and higher earnings the rest. The improvement for creditors rests mainly on sale proceeds applied to debt, not on a change in the earnings base.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C05; calculation C12

The earnings improvement is real but includes items that do not recur. Last-twelve-months EBITDA includes a patent settlement gain of USD 25.0 million and a tariff refund benefit of USD 25.3 million, about 11.95% of that EBITDA; without them net leverage would be 3.21x, an Analyst Judgement shown in the register and not used in any fixed row. FY2025 earnings, by contrast, carry a non-cash asset impairment and a currency hedge gain, but both sit in FY2025 and in the nine months of 2025, so they cancel out of the last-twelve-months figure. The strongest contrary evidence is the rise in reported gross margin to 59.8% in nine months 2026 from 57.1%, which the issuer attributes mainly to lower VI Business inventory step-up charges and to the tariff refunds; the step-up fade is durable but the refunds are not, and a fourth quarter without one-off gains would settle how much of the improvement lasts.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C11

Interest cover on cash interest is modest and cannot be updated. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.48x in FY2025 against 2.70x in FY2024, and accrued interest expense, which is lower because swap interest benefits reduce it, was covered 2.95x and 3.18x. On the same accrued basis last-twelve-months cover is 4.09x, which reflects both higher earnings and lower debt after the sale proceeds. Nine-month cash interest paid is not stated, so a 2026 cash cover cannot be built.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 141; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 109; calculation C06

Cash generation improved but shareholder returns absorbed more than it. Last-twelve-months free cash flow after capital expenditure is positive and far above FY2025, which was close to zero after a build-up of receivables and higher tax payments, but it includes the patent settlement and tariff refunds in operating cash flow. In nine months 2026 cash paid for share repurchases was 3.08 times free cash flow, so the OEM sale proceeds also went to shareholders as well as to debt, and a further USD 41.4 million was repurchased after the quarter end. The remaining repurchase authorization means further payouts could slow deleveraging.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C10

Liquidity is adequate against near-term debt but is not fully measured. Cash plus the undrawn revolver before letters of credit is large against the USD 87.5 million of borrowings due within 12 months, and the securitization program has USD 75.0 million drawn, the maximum stated at year-end 2025. Income taxes payable rose by USD 175.851 million over the nine months, and the issuer expects to fund cash taxes on the OEM gain from the revolver and cash in the fourth quarter, which will reduce liquidity and raise net debt by an amount the filing does not state. The nearest dated bullet maturity is the 2028 notes of USD 500.0 million, and the May 2026 refinancing moved the revolver and Term A-1 to 2031; the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale, expected to bring about USD 530 million gross, would lower net debt if it closes, and closing may slip into 2027.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C12

No non-debt funding float of size was identified: the filings disclose no supplier finance, factoring, deferred revenue or customer deposits, and the receivables securitization is inside debt. The OEM sale is a multi-figure event whose roles are kept apart: net cash proceeds of USD 1.5 billion, after-tax proceeds of USD 1.3 billion in the latest report, a pre-tax gain recognised in discontinued operations, and an investing inflow in the cash flow statement; the June 2026 report gave a lower after-tax figure and the later report controls.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 34

## Findings
### Bottom line

Teleflex is shrinking into a narrower vascular, interventional and surgical device group, and creditors now depend on new leadership splitting sale proceeds between bank debt repayment and share buybacks, the two uses management named.

The retained franchise is profitable: nine-month segment operating profit rose 20.0% and the bank facilities now run to 2031. Against that, 2026 growth was bought through the BIOTRONIK acquisition, the chief executive, Chair and board all changed during 2026, an activist wants strategic alternatives reviewed, and the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale has slipped towards 2027.

### Key findings

The business creditors keep is smaller, and about three quarters of its 2026 revenue growth was bought rather than earned. Continuing operations were 60.44% of FY2025 combined net revenues, with the other 39.56% sold or held for sale. Net revenues rose 18.4% in the nine months of 2026, but USD 198.1 million of the USD 262.7 million increase, or 75.41%, came from the BIOTRONIK business bought on 2025-06-30, and third-quarter revenue rose only 0.2%.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C01; calculation C04

Interventional is the growth engine and the weak point. It supplied 37.17% of nine-month segment revenue after the acquisition, yet its segment margin was 10.37% against 14.10% a year earlier, its third-quarter revenue fell 2.6%, and its fair value exceeded carrying value by only about 15%, a cushion that a 1% rise in the discount rate would cut to below 5%. A further shortfall in the acquired business would first appear as an impairment signal.

Governance changed on every front in 2026, and the filings do not yet state how the new board will weigh creditors against shareholders. The Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer left on 2026-01-08, an interim chief executive served for five months and a new one started on 2026-06-08; an independent Chair was appointed on 2026-01-08 and replaced on 2026-05-15; two directors left on 2026-05-15 and three joined, on 2026-05-15, 2026-06-08 and 2026-09-08; and an activist called for board changes and a review of strategic alternatives on 2026-03-27. No leverage target or credit rating is stated, and the proxy statement with board and ownership detail was not supplied.

Management has said shareholders will share in the sale proceeds, and its 2026 actions are mixed rather than adverse. The 2025 annual report and the first-quarter 2026 report said the expected net after-tax proceeds of about USD 1.8 billion would be used "primarily to return capital to shareholders through share repurchases and pay down debt", and the later reports do not repeat the statement. After the OEM sale closed on 2026-08-03 the company repaid USD 1,190.0 million of bank debt, and from 2026-07-01 to the report date it also repurchased USD 350.0 million of stock, so repayment was 3.40 times repurchases in that window. Since 2026-01-01 repurchases total USD 600.0 million, USD 400.0 million of the USD 1.0 billion authorisation remains, and the dividend is USD 0.34 per share a quarter.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is what management has done with cash. It repaid the USD 700.0 million Term A-2 loan and USD 490.0 million of the revolver within weeks of the OEM closing, extended the revolver and Term A-1 to 2031, redeemed the 2027 notes, and raised segment operating profit 20.0% in nine months with Vascular up 16.5% and Surgical up 34.3%. No acquisition, extraordinary dividend or creditor-adverse transaction is disclosed after 2025, repurchases to date are smaller than debt repayment, and the dividend is unchanged at USD 0.34 per share.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C07

The view would turn more cautious if the Acute Care and Interventional Urology proceeds, or the remaining USD 400.0 million authorisation and a larger one, went mainly to buybacks while the fourth-quarter taxes are drawn on the revolver; if the Palette claim succeeds above the contingent consideration liability; if the Acute Care sale slips beyond 2027 or fails; or if the review of strategic alternatives the activist wants ends in a sale of the company, which could engage the notes' repurchase right on a change of control if a ratings downgrade accompanies it. It would improve if the new chief executive states a leverage policy, if sale proceeds are applied to debt, and if the guarantor perimeter and segment reporting stop changing.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Three transaction streams define the credit. In 2025 Teleflex bought the BIOTRONIK vascular intervention business, completed on 2025-06-30 for a net initial cash payment of EUR 704.3 million, or USD 825.2 million, against an agreed initial price of EUR 760 million before adjustments, funded with USD 700 million of delayed draw term loan borrowings and USD 140 million drawn on the revolver. On 2025-12-09 it signed agreements to sell the OEM business to Montagu and Kohlberg and the Acute Care and Interventional Urology businesses to Intersurgical for USD 2.0 billion in cash in total, about USD 1.5 billion and USD 530 million respectively. In 2026 it refinanced its bank debt and its 2027 notes and repaid bank debt from the OEM proceeds.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 40; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Low: The revenue and earnings of the OEM, Acute Care and Interventional Urology businesses are not split in the 2025 and 2026 reports, and the employee count at 2025-12-31 may include them; the company could supply the split.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit analysis of Teleflex Inc (issuer tfx-96943), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the continuing company after the 2026 sales: business risk, cash-flow durability, leverage, liquidity, refinancing and financial policy, drawn from the 2024 and 2025 annual reports, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the supplied Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses. Legal and covenant basket analysis, recovery waterfalls, relative value and position sizing are outside this analysis.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-28 | c7ca355ac9a894aec94427874e1c591385211de097514ece22017a538ff864f4 | Company history, the separation plan announced 2025-02-27 and the Palette purchase terms. |

| Supplied analysis | Module | sha256 | Use |

The run settings leave sector, country and sponsor blank; they are not issuer evidence and none is treated as zero. A retrieval record found beside the filings is not a source.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Teleflex is an adequate credit that has improved through asset sales more than through earnings, and creditors now depend on how management splits the proceeds still to come between debt and shareholders. Net leverage was 2.82x at 2026-09-30 against 7.64x at year-end 2025 on a narrower earnings base. It is 2.92x after USD 41.4 million of later repurchases and 1.56x if the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale closes at about USD 530 million, while the effect of fourth-quarter taxes on the OEM gain is not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C12

The retained business turned 57.71% of last-twelve-months EBITDA into free cash flow and has no note maturity before 2028-06-01, but USD 50.3 million of one-off gains sits in last-twelve-months EBITDA, shareholder payments were 2.53 times free cash flow, and covenant headroom is not reported.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43; calculation C05; calculation C07; calculation C11
### Key findings

Leverage is moderate because debt was repaid, not because earnings grew, and the ratio depends on the earnings base. After the OEM sale closed Teleflex repaid USD 700.0 million of Term A-2 and USD 490.0 million of the revolver, yet the 2.82x reported net leverage becomes 4.01x on FY2025 EBITDA and 3.21x without USD 50.3 million of settlement and tariff-refund gains. On the reported basis the pro forma readings are 2.92x after USD 41.4 million of repurchases made after 2026-09-30 and 1.56x if the sale for about USD 530 million closes; the OEM tax effect is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C11; calculation C12

Earnings improved, but more than a tenth of last-twelve-months EBITDA is one-off. The EBITDA margin is 18.67% against 14.86% in FY2025, yet the USD 25.0 million patent settlement gain and USD 25.3 million of tariff refunds are 11.95% of EBITDA, and without them the margin is 16.44% and nine-month gross margin is 58.27% instead of the reported 59.8%. Further tariff refunds may arrive in the fourth quarter but no receivable is recorded, and quality remediation and excess inventory charges already weigh on gross margin.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44; calculation C11

The retained core earns well, but Interventional is the swing factor for earnings. Vascular and Surgical earned segment margins of 38.12% and 45.10% and grew nine-month revenue 7.2% and 8.4% without acquisitions, while Interventional earned 10.37%, saw third-quarter revenue fall 2.6%, and has a goodwill cushion of about 15% that a 1% rise in the discount rate would cut below 5%. Its profit is 13.21% of segment profit but 32.77% of nine-month operating income after unallocated costs, so losing all of it would cut operating income by about a third, although segment profit would still be 4.11% above the nine-month 2025 total.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation C03

Cash conversion is solid, but shareholder payments outran it. Last-twelve-months free cash flow was USD 242.99 million, 57.71% of EBITDA, on capital spending of only 3.47% of net revenues, yet dividends and repurchases took 2.53 times that amount. Nine-month operating cash flow also benefited from lower tax payments, vendor payment timing and receipts from the settlement and refunds, which may not repeat.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07

Liquidity and maturities are comfortable, and the open questions are cost and covenant headroom. Only USD 87.5 million of borrowings fall due within 12 months, cash alone equals 86.09% of the USD 500.0 million of notes due 2028-06-01, the undrawn revolver is up to USD 940 million before letters of credit, and the revolver and Term A-1 now mature on 2031-05-26. EBITDA covers the run-rate coupon cost of the debt outstanding 5.04x, or 4.43x without the one-offs, and floating-rate debt is 38.72% of principal against 62.26% at 2025-12-31; the replaced 2027 notes cost 1.25 percentage points less than the new 2032 notes.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10

Financial policy is the main unknown. No leverage target or agency rating is stated, the chief executive and the Chair changed in 2026, three directors joined and two left, and an activist wants strategic alternatives reviewed. Since 2026-07-01 Teleflex repaid 3.40 times as much bank debt as it spent on stock, but USD 400.0 million of the repurchase authorisation remains and the programme may be suspended at any time, so the commitment to debt is a record, not a rule.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 60

The business profile is adequate rather than strong. Nine-month net revenues were USD 1,686.4 million, and continuing operations are 60.44% of FY2025 combined revenue; about three quarters of nine-month growth was acquired, no customer concentration or market share is disclosed, and 42.91% of nine-month revenue comes from outside North America, where most customer relationships outside the United States are with government entities. Against that, substantially all revenue is single-use devices used in high-acuity procedures, and existing-product volumes rose USD 37.7 million.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C01
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is what management did with the first proceeds and what the retained segments earn. It repaid USD 1,190.0 million of bank debt against USD 350.0 million of repurchases since 2026-07-01, pushed bank maturities to 2031-05-26, grew segment operating profit 20.0% in nine months, and today covers run-rate interest 5.04x. The strongest evidence for a weaker view is the fourth-quarter OEM tax payment, the unstated financial policy, and earnings that carry 11.95% of one-offs.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; calculation C08; calculation C11

The view would improve if the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale closes and its proceeds reduce the revolver, if management states a leverage target, if fourth-quarter free cash flow holds without one-off receipts, and if covenant ratios are reported with clear headroom. It would weaken if the revolver rises above USD 60.0 million at year-end to pay taxes while repurchases continue under the USD 400.0 million authorisation, if Interventional revenue keeps falling and an impairment follows, if the Acute Care sale fails or slips beyond 2027, or if the strategic review ends in a sale of the company.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 60
### Limitations

- No Credit Agreement compliance statement, covenant ratio or letters of credit figure is reported for 2026, so the conclusion that liquidity and maturities are comfortable cannot be tested against headroom and the undrawn revolver is an upper bound.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54

- The company states no EBITDA, so every leverage, cover and cash conversion figure rests on a derivation from statement lines, and the conclusion that earnings improved would change if the company's own measure differs.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The amount of the cash taxes on the OEM gain is not stated, so the conclusion that leverage is moderate could weaken by an amount the filings do not give, and no pro forma figure for it can be built.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1)
- No agency rating, leverage target or management forecast is in the supplied filings, so the adequate profile and the outlook are analyst judgements without an external anchor.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The competitive-strength reading rests on the company's own risk factors and reported margins, with no competitor, price or share series, so it could change if external data show the retained franchises gaining or losing share.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 18

- The downside path is built from disclosed sensitivities and segment shares rather than a forecast, so it shows the order of events and their relative size but not the likelihood or the final level of leverage.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation C03
### Source gate and readiness

Module status is Ready with Limitations. All five filings and the three supplied analyses are present, name Teleflex Inc and agree on the perimeter: continuing operations only, with the OEM business sold on 2026-08-03 and the Acute Care and Interventional Urology businesses held for sale. What is missing is the proxy statement, the executed credit, note and sale agreements, Credit Agreement compliance figures and letters of credit; each restricts only the conclusion named in Limitations or Gaps, and none blocks the analysis.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54

The datapoints taken from Financial foundation are last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 421.027 million, net debt of USD 1,188.491 million and cash of USD 430.465 million at 2026-09-30, reported net leverage of 2.82x, and last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 242.99 million. Its post-balance-sheet table gives net leverage of 2.92x after USD 41.4 million of repurchases made after 2026-09-30 and 1.56x if the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale closes for about USD 530 million; it states no figure for the cash taxes on the OEM gain, so that effect is not established. All of these are carried unchanged.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12
### Company description

Teleflex is a Delaware company founded in 1943 that sells single-use critical care and surgical devices to hospitals through direct sales forces, independent representatives and distributors, and it reports three continuing segments. Vascular (Arrow catheters, EZ-IO intraosseous access, QuikClot hemostats) was 46.05% of FY2025 continuing net revenues, Interventional (coronary and peripheral catheters, GuideLiner, MANTA and, since 2025-06-30, BIOTRONIK drug-coated balloons and stents) was 32.51% and Surgical (ligating clips, fascial closure, a powered bariatric stapler) was 20.98%; by the nine months of 2026 Interventional had grown to 37.17% of segment net revenues. Substantially all revenue is single-use devices used in high-acuity procedures, so revenue recurs with procedure volumes, but most orders ship within days or weeks, backlog gives no visibility, and sales are highest in the fourth quarter. The credit consequence is a base of consumable demand with short visibility rather than contracted revenue.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 39; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13

The company is much smaller than the one the debt was raised against. Continuing operations are 60.44% of FY2025 combined net revenues, because the OEM business was sold for net cash proceeds of USD 1.5 billion on 2026-08-03 and the Acute Care and Interventional Urology businesses are agreed to be sold for about USD 530 million but had not closed by 2026-11-05. The disposals replaced a plan announced on 2025-02-27 to separate those businesses into a new listed company, and the BIOTRONIK purchase of 2025-06-30 for USD 825.2 million added the growth segment. Portfolio changes of this size make earlier leverage and margin series poor guides, so the analysis uses the recast continuing figures only.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2024-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; calculation C13

Cyclicality is limited. Demand follows hospital procedure counts, with elective procedures and flu seasons moving the quarterly pattern, and the one disclosed structural demand loss is bariatric surgery, where the adoption of GLP-1 products reduced demand and led to a USD 100.0 million impairment of the Titan SGS asset group in 2025. Regulation is a barrier and a cost: products are mainly Class I and Class II devices cleared through the FDA 510(k) process, the European Union Medical Device Regulation certification is expected to complete in 2026, and the FDA quality system regulation was replaced on 2026-02-02. No customer, distributor or group purchasing concentration is disclosed, so concentration risk is neither found nor ruled out.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 46
### Ownership and group structure

Teleflex is publicly held and is its own reporting entity, so issuer and group are the same company. No controlling holder, sponsor or parent is named, 315 holders of record were reported at 2026-02-24, and the activist Irenic Capital Management called on 2026-03-27 for board changes and an evaluation of strategic alternatives without a stated stake. Financial policy is therefore set by a board and management that changed substantially in 2026: the chief executive left on 2026-01-08, an interim served until Jason Weidman started on 2026-06-08, and the independent Chair changed on 2026-01-08 and again on 2026-05-15. The credit consequence is that policy is neither anchored by an owner with a stated leverage tolerance nor yet tested by the new team.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 60; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Debt sits at the parent. Substantially all material domestic subsidiaries guarantee the Credit Agreement and both note series, each guarantor is directly or indirectly 100% owned, and the bank facilities are secured by a lien on substantially all assets of the company and each guarantor; the security of the notes is not stated and the guarantors are not listed in the filings. The share of assets and earnings outside the guarantor group is not established, and the receivables securitization vehicle is bankruptcy-remote, so its assets are not available to the parent's other creditors. Obligor group total assets at 2025-12-31 were restated twice, from USD 2,797.8 million to USD 2,831.2 million and then to USD 5,011.1 million, so guarantor-level comparisons across reports are not reliable.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 141; calculation C16

Financial policy is visible only in actions. The quarterly dividend is USD 0.34 per share, the board authorised USD 1.0 billion of repurchases on 2025-12-09 of which USD 400.0 million remains, and management said in the 2025 annual report and the first-quarter 2026 report that expected net after-tax proceeds of about USD 1.8 billion would be used primarily to return capital through repurchases and to pay down debt, a statement the later reports do not repeat. The Credit Agreement limits dividends and other restricted payments subject to thresholds, and the note indentures as summarised limit liens, mergers and sale-leasebacks without mentioning restricted payments, but neither document is supplied, so the capacity to return cash is not established. Creditor alignment is partial: repayment so far exceeds repurchases, but nothing binds the remaining proceeds.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C07
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue growth is mostly acquired and the organic base grows slowly. Of the USD 262.7 million rise in nine-month net revenues, USD 198.1 million came from the BIOTRONIK business, USD 37.7 million from higher volumes of existing products and the remaining USD 26.9 million from price, currency and new products; against a base of USD 1,423.7 million these are 13.91, 2.65 and 1.89 percentage points of the 18.45% rise. Existing-product volumes and selective price increases are the repeatable organic drivers, and volume growth of 2.65% for nine months cannot by itself change leverage quickly.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C01

The latest quarter shows the stall. Third-quarter net revenues rose 0.2% to USD 567.8 million, helped by USD 6.0 million of volume and by price increases and held back by a prior-year reserve release under the Italian payback measure of USD 9.035 million that did not recur; segment net revenues, which exclude that release, rose 1.8%. Vascular grew 4.7% on volume and price, Surgical grew 4.2% on volume, new products and price, and Interventional fell 2.6% on lower volume and price decreases, so pricing power is selective: it is positive in Vascular and Surgical and negative in the acquired Interventional business.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; calculation C02

Government and cost-containment pressure is the structural price risk. Most customer relationships outside the United States are with government entities, 42.91% of nine-month revenue was earned outside North America, and the annual report says cost containment, collective purchasing, competitive bidding and tenders, including China's volume-based procurement, may exert downward pressure on pricing. Customer concentration, contract duration, renewal rates and switching costs are not disclosed, and the company names only the Teleflex name and the Arrow brand as essential intellectual property, so durability rests on clinical use and regulatory barriers rather than on patents or contracts.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation C13

Revenue is recurring, regulated and mostly non-discretionary, partly cyclical through elective procedures, exposed to government pricing and to one demonstrated substitution risk, and not structurally declining in the retained segments. The weaker link is growth, which was bought, so revenue durability supports base cash flow but gives little organic deleveraging.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02
### Cost structure and margin resilience

The reported margin gain is partly one-off. Nine-month gross margin was 59.8% against 57.1%, helped by lower inventory step-up charges from the BIOTRONIK acquisition and by a USD 25.3 million benefit from refunds of tariffs that a court invalidated on 2026-02-20, and held back by quality remediation and excess and obsolete inventory charges; without the refund the gross margin is 58.27%. In the prior-year third quarter Interventional cost of goods sold was USD 123.1 million on USD 216.0 million of revenue against USD 83.4 million on USD 210.3 million in 2026, so part of the improvement is a base effect rather than efficiency.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C03; calculation C11

Operating expenses rose faster than revenue. Selling, general and administrative expense was 39.2% of nine-month revenue against 35.0%, mainly because a prior-year gain of USD 87.1 million on foreign exchange forwards hedging the BIOTRONIK price did not recur and the acquired business adds operating, integration and amortization costs; research and development rose to 7.9% from 6.7% on Interventional project spend. Operating leverage shows in the segments: Vascular profit rose 16.5% on revenue up 7.2% and Surgical profit rose 34.3% on revenue up 8.4%, while Interventional profit rose only 7.3% on revenue up 45.8%. The same leverage works in reverse, so a revenue decline in a high-margin segment would cut profit faster than revenue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50

Cost actions are large relative to the earnings they are meant to protect. Three restructuring plans carry aggregate charges of USD 79 million to USD 96 million and expected annual savings of USD 74 million to USD 86 million, the company expects most or all of the charges of the two larger plans to be cash, USD 15 million to USD 19 million of cash costs are expected in 2026 under the plan tied to the sales, and the plans run to 2027 and 2028 with some savings dependent on exit from transition agreements with the buyers. Until they are delivered, stranded costs left by the sold businesses are a drag whose size is not disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C15

Input-cost exposure is real but unquantified. The annual report says commodity price and freight cost volatility can have a significant impact on production cost and that alternative sources of materials and sterilization can be delayed by regulatory requirements, and the third-quarter report adds energy price and supply chain risk from the Middle East conflict. No pass-through mechanism, fixed-cost share or price indexation is disclosed, so the ability to defend margin under cost inflation is not established; the evidence of defended margin is the price increases in Vascular and Surgical in 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50

Margins can be defended under modest volume pressure because gross margin is high, but this is not demonstrated under input cost inflation or adverse mix. The 29.19% segment margin overstates group profitability: unallocated items, which include corporate costs and manufacturing variances, absorbed 56.28% of segment profit in nine months against 46.51% a year earlier, and income before interest and taxes was 11.77% of nine-month revenue, so margin resilience is better read on the group EBITDA margin of 18.67% over the last twelve months.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C03
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is low, which limits investment risk but leaves little to cut. Capital expenditure was USD 54.4 million in nine months, 3.23% of net revenues against 5.02% a year earlier and 3.47% over the last twelve months, while depreciation and amortization were 9.20% of nine-month revenue because of acquired intangibles. Capital spending is already a small cash call, so reducing it is a weak lever in a downturn.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 38; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06

Conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow is volatile. It was 39.26% in FY2023, 79.73% in FY2024, 0.49% in FY2025 after a build-up of receivables and higher tax payments, and 57.71% over the last twelve months; nine-month free cash flow was USD 180.4 million against a negative USD 61.1 million a year earlier. Without the USD 50.3 million of settlement and refund receipts, last-twelve-months free cash flow would be USD 192.69 million before tax effects, or 51.98% of EBITDA without the one-offs.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C05

Cash uses compete with debt service. Cash interest paid was USD 119.337 million in FY2025, while accrued interest expense fell to USD 21.2 million in the third quarter from USD 31.8 million as debt was repaid and the average interest rate on debt fell to 3.5% from 4.1%. Financial foundation's last-twelve-months cover on accrued interest is 4.09x, below the 5.04x on run-rate coupon cost because it includes interest on debt repaid in August. Dividends were USD 58.774 million and repurchases USD 554.951 million over the last twelve months, together 2.53 times free cash flow, restructuring cash costs and the fourth-quarter OEM taxes are still to come, and income taxes payable were USD 194.638 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 18.787 million at year-end 2025. Noncurrent operating lease liabilities of USD 60.785 million are outside the debt figures.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C07; calculation C14

EBITDA translates into free cash flow sufficient for debt service and moderate deleveraging at present levels, but only about half of EBITDA is kept as free cash flow before shareholder payments, and receipts that may not repeat and working-capital timing flatter the latest figure. Debt service capacity is sound; the open question is how much free cash flow goes to shareholders.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C07
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense and shows first in Interventional. The annual report calls the industry highly competitive, with competitors from start-ups to larger and better-funded companies, and says Teleflex competes on clinical superiority, reliability, support and cost-effectiveness; no competitor is named and no share is given. The numbers show rivalry in Interventional price decreases and lower volumes in the third quarter while Vascular and Surgical raised prices, so the threat falls on the acquired segment's 10.37% margin and on the goodwill cushion that rests on it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C03

The threat of new entrants is moderate. Regulatory clearance, European Union certification, quality system rules and hospital relationships limit entry, but the company says no single patent is essential beyond the Teleflex name and the Arrow brand, and its USD 25.0 million patent settlement in April 2026 shows both the value of its intellectual property and the need to defend it. Entry would reach creditors through price, so it is a margin risk.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 42

The threat of substitutes is concentrated in bariatric surgery. The Titan SGS bariatric stapler faced reduced demand as GLP-1 products spread and was impaired by USD 100.0 million in 2025; the filings name no other substitution threat to the retained products, and Surgical revenue still grew 8.4% in nine months. The risk is bounded: further impairment would be non-cash, but a broader shift away from procedures would cut volume in a segment that earned a 45.10% margin.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; calculation C03

Buyer power is high in government-funded markets. Hospitals buy through direct sales forces, representatives and distributors, most customer relationships outside the United States are with government entities, and governments use price controls, collective purchasing, competitive bidding and tenders, with China's volume-based procurement named as an adverse influence on future pricing; concentration among buyers is not disclosed. The consequence is a cap on price increases in the 42.91% of revenue earned outside North America, which makes price a less reliable offset to cost inflation there.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C13

Supplier power is low to moderate. Materials, components and sterilization services come from many suppliers and no single supplier is substantial, yet the risk language names sole-source suppliers and sterilization providers, regulatory requirements can delay alternative sources, and a contract sterilizer whose ethylene oxide plants at two sites have faced legal proceedings has sterilized some vascular and surgical products. A suspension at those plants could interrupt supply of the affected products, which is a revenue and working-capital risk more than a margin risk.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 57
### Macro and policy factors

PEST factors are a material credit driver here, because tariffs, foreign currency, government pricing and regulation each move margin, cash flow or refinancing cost, so the four categories are assessed.

Political and regulatory factors work through tariffs and pricing rules. A court decision on 2026-02-20 invalidated the tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, replacement tariffs were imposed under other authority, and Teleflex received refunds that gave a USD 25.3 million benefit in continuing operations and USD 13.9 million in discontinued operations; more refund requests are expected in the fourth quarter with no receivable recorded, and the scope and durability of the replacement tariffs are uncertain. Gross margin and cash flow therefore carry tariff risk in both directions. Regulatory cost is shifting rather than rising: European Union Medical Device Regulation costs fell in the third quarter, the FDA quality system rule was replaced on 2026-02-02, and European Union certification is expected to complete in 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16

Economic factors work through currency, interest rates and energy. About 42.91% of nine-month revenue was earned outside North America, the principal currency exposures are the euro, Chinese renminbi, Mexican peso, Malaysian ringgit, Swiss franc and Canadian dollar, and Teleflex hedges with forward contracts of USD 547.3 million of notional and cross-currency swaps of USD 1.6 billion of notional at 2025-12-31, the swaps being designated as net investment hedges. A 10% rise in the dollar would raise the fair value of the hedge contracts by USD 179.5 million and a 10% fall would cut it by USD 182.2 million at that date. Floating-rate debt is 38.72% of principal, so a 1.0 percentage point rise in rates would add USD 6.32 million a year to interest cost, and the Middle East conflict is cited as a source of energy price and supply chain risk.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C09; calculation C13

Social and technological factors are secondary. Social factors matter only through treatment shifts that change procedure demand, and the single disclosed case is the adoption of GLP-1 products, which reduced bariatric demand. Technology is not a primary credit driver on the evidence: research and development is 7.9% of nine-month revenue, the acquired business adds drug-coated balloons, stents and catheters, and no disruptive technology threat to the core single-use products is stated, although Interventional development spend must keep the acquired franchise competitive.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 45
### SWOT in credit terms

Strengths are recurring single-use device demand, high gross margin, low capital intensity with positive free cash flow, a debt stack with no note maturity before 2028-06-01 after the bank facilities were extended to 2031-05-26, and Vascular and Surgical margins of 38.12% and 45.10%. Each supports debt service because it keeps cash generation inside the business and leaves the first large maturity distant.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C03; calculation C06

Weaknesses are an Interventional segment with a 10.37% margin and a thin goodwill cushion, USD 50.3 million of one-off gains in EBITDA, an unstated financial policy with shareholder payments above free cash flow, a smaller company after the sales with stranded costs still to be removed, and a board and management team in transition. Each reduces the reliability of the leverage reached so far.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C03; calculation C11

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are application of the roughly USD 530 million Acute Care sale proceeds to the revolver, annual restructuring savings of USD 74 million to USD 86 million, a recovery of Interventional margin toward the 14.10% of a year earlier as integration completes, further tariff refunds, and lower interest cost as floating-rate debt reprices.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C03; calculation C15

Threats that could weaken credit quality are fourth-quarter OEM taxes and repurchases funded on the revolver, tariff and government pricing changes, further GLP-1 effects on Surgical, a sterilization supply interruption, and an activist-driven strategic review that ends in a sale or a recapitalization.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 35
### Strengths and weaknesses
The five strongest credit supports, in order of weight, follow.

Low capital intensity and positive free cash flow carry debt service from operations. Capital spending is 3.47% of net revenues and last-twelve-months free cash flow was USD 242.99 million, 57.71% of EBITDA, so interest and scheduled repayments are met without refinancing; the caveat is that conversion has swung between 0.49% and 79.73% over recent years.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06

Vascular and Surgical earn high margins and grow without acquisitions. Segment margins of 38.12% and 45.10% on revenue growth of 7.2% and 8.4% in nine months give operating leverage on volume and price, which lets the core carry the debt while Interventional is repaired.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; calculation C03

Debt was cut and maturities were extended. Principal fell by USD 1,018.125 million to USD 1,631.875 million, the revolver and Term A-1 now run to 2031-05-26, and the first note maturity is USD 500.0 million on 2028-06-01, so no refinancing event is due in the next 12 months beyond USD 87.5 million of current borrowings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation C14

Interest cost is covered with room. EBITDA covers the run-rate coupon cost of the debt outstanding 5.04x, or 4.43x without the one-offs, and floating-rate debt fell to 38.72% of principal, which limits rate sensitivity to USD 6.32 million a year for each percentage point.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C08; calculation C09

Demand is for consumable devices used in high-acuity procedures, and existing-product volumes grew in 2026. A USD 37.7 million rise in nine-month volumes supports base cash flow visibility, although it is only 2.65% of the prior-year base.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C01
The five most material credit weaknesses, in order of weight, follow.

Financial policy is unstated and shareholder payments exceed free cash flow. Dividends and repurchases took 2.53 times last-twelve-months free cash flow, USD 400.0 million of authorisation remains, no leverage target is stated and the board and management changed in 2026, so leverage is a result of the first proceeds and not a commitment.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C07

Interventional margin, volume and goodwill cushion are weak. The segment earned 10.37% against 14.10%, revenue fell 2.6% in the third quarter, the goodwill cushion is about 15% and a 1% rise in the discount rate would cut it below 5%, and its profit is 32.77% of nine-month operating income, so a shortfall would reach earnings and book equity at once.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation C03

Earnings carry one-offs and temporary support. USD 50.3 million of settlement and tariff-refund gains are 11.95% of EBITDA, and nine-month operating cash flow benefited from lower tax payments and vendor payment timing, so underlying leverage is higher than the reported ratio.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C11

The fourth-quarter OEM taxes and the Acute Care sale timing leave net debt open. Taxes on the gain are to be funded from the revolver and cash in an amount not stated, income taxes payable rose to USD 194.638 million from USD 18.787 million, and the sale for about USD 530 million may close only in 2027.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54

The company is smaller and still being reshaped. Continuing operations are 60.44% of FY2025 combined net revenues, about three quarters of nine-month growth was acquired, and three restructuring plans with charges of USD 79 million to USD 96 million run to 2028, so scale, stranded cost and integration execution are unproven.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C01; calculation C13; calculation C15
### Financial profile and credit quality

The main credit supports are cash generation, liquidity and maturity profile, not scale or diversification. The business earns an 18.67% EBITDA margin on last-twelve-months net revenues, converts 57.71% of EBITDA into free cash flow with low capital spending, holds cash equal to 86.09% of the 2028 notes, and has bank maturities in 2031; its reporting is regular and audited and no sponsor controls it. The consequence is that debt service is supported by operations rather than by asset sales alone, even though the leverage fall came from sales.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; calculation C05; calculation C10

The main constraints are earnings quality, the Interventional drag and unstated policy. Reported net leverage of 2.82x at 2026-09-30 compares with 4.01x on FY2025 EBITDA and 3.21x without USD 50.3 million of one-offs, and the pro forma positions of that headline are 2.92x after USD 41.4 million of repurchases made after 2026-09-30 and 1.56x if the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale closes for about USD 530 million, while the effect of the fourth-quarter OEM taxes is not established. The covenant levels in the Credit Agreement are a maximum net leverage of 4.50x and a minimum interest coverage of 3.00x, but the filings report no ratio against them for 2026 and define neither in terms that allow a computation here, so headroom is not calculable.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C18

The trend is better on cash flow and worse on comparability. Net leverage on the reported basis was 5.31x at 2024-12-31, 7.64x at 2025-12-31 and 2.82x at 2026-09-30, but the year-end ratios divide consolidated debt that also financed the sold businesses by continuing earnings only, so the improvement overstates the change. EBITDA margin was 23.76% in FY2023, 15.60% in FY2024, 14.86% in FY2025 and 18.67% over the last twelve months, and cash interest cover was 4.06x, 2.70x and 2.48x for FY2023 to FY2025; the last twelve months have no cash cover because nine-month cash interest paid is not stated.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)

Missing datapoints that would make the opinion more definitive are the covenant compliance calculation and the Credit Agreement definitions, letters of credit outstanding, the amount of the OEM taxes, the securitization maturity and the Term A-1 amortization schedule, a leverage target and agency rating, management guidance, and the split of earnings between the sold and retained businesses.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

The 12 to 24 month outlook is dominated by dated events. The fourth quarter brings the OEM tax payment, seasonally higher sales, possible further tariff refunds and the restructuring savings that are due to begin in 2026; by the end of 2026 or in 2027 the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale should close for about USD 530 million; on the usual twelve-month classification rule the notes due 2028-06-01 would become a current liability at the 2027-06-30 balance sheet if they are not refinanced. For creditors the near term decides whether leverage settles near the reported level or drifts, depending on how the revolver, repurchases and the sale proceeds interact.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54

The three to five year outlook turns on integration, savings and refinancing. The BIOTRONIK integration plan runs to the end of 2028 and the plan tied to the sales to mid-2028, the 2028 notes mature in 2028-06-01 and the bank facilities and Term A-1 in 2031-05-26, and the 2032 notes mature on 2032-01-15. Sustained margin recovery in Interventional and delivery of the USD 74 million to USD 86 million of annual savings would lift cash generation, while a failure of either would leave leverage dependent on asset sales that have already been made.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C15

Tailwinds are company-specific more than sector-wide. Existing-product volumes grew USD 37.7 million, prices rose in Vascular and Surgical, accrued interest cost is falling with debt and the average rate on debt, and savings and tariff refunds may add cash; each supports revenue, margin or cash flow visibility, though none is large enough to change deleveraging alone.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50

Headwinds are pricing, tariffs, substitution and execution. Government price controls and tenders, replacement tariffs, GLP-1 effects on bariatric demand, quality remediation costs, stranded costs and an activist-driven review each pressure margin, volume or financial policy, and the first two are sector-wide while the rest are specific to Teleflex.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 60
### Downside scenario

The scenario is Interventional keeping the third-quarter pattern while the fourth-quarter taxes and further repurchases are drawn on the revolver. The initiating condition is that Interventional revenue, which fell 2.6% in the third quarter on lower volume and price decreases, stays weak at a 10.37% margin. The first operational break is that the acquired business fails to hold its revenue base; with a goodwill cushion of about 15% that a 1% rise in the discount rate would cut below 5%, the first financial signal would be an impairment test on goodwill and intangibles of USD 3,693.068 million, 58.18% of total assets and 105.71% of equity, a non-cash charge against equity that already has no tangible cushion, since equity less goodwill and intangibles is negative USD 199.352 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation C03; calculation C04

The financial transmission is through earnings and cash. Interventional produces 32.77% of nine-month operating income, and the USD 50.3 million of one-off gains, 11.95% of EBITDA, would not recur, so leverage would move toward the without-one-offs reading of 3.21x before any operating loss; all leverage readings here use net debt at 2026-09-30, and the pro forma positions of 2.92x and 1.56x and the unstated OEM tax effect are set out in the financial profile above. The liquidity and refinancing consequence is limited in the next two years: cash and the undrawn revolver of up to USD 940 million cover the notes due 2028-06-01, of USD 500.0 million, 2.74 times, but the next refinancing would be priced off a weaker earnings record, and the covenant tests of 4.50x net leverage and 3.00x interest coverage cannot be checked against reported ratios.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation C03; calculation C10; calculation C11

Management has levers, and they are enough to avoid liquidity distress on the disclosed figures. It can suspend repurchases, since USD 400.0 million remains and the programme may be suspended at any time, hold the dividend, which costs about USD 53.94 million a year at the current share count and is 22.20% of last-twelve-months free cash flow, realise restructuring savings, and apply the Acute Care proceeds to the revolver. Free cash flow after dividends was USD 184.216 million over the last twelve months, so the realistic failure mode is slow leverage creep and loss of policy credibility, not default. The observable triggers are a revolver balance above USD 60.0 million at 2026-12-31, Interventional revenue and margin in the fourth quarter, any goodwill impairment charge, the pace of repurchases and the covenant disclosure in the next annual report.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C07
### Overall credit view

Overall, Teleflex presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring single-use device demand, high Vascular and Surgical margins, low capital intensity and no note maturity before 2028-06-01, but credit quality is constrained by acquired rather than organic growth, a thin and impairment-sensitive Interventional segment, earnings that include USD 50.3 million of one-offs, shareholder payments of 2.53 times free cash flow and an unstated financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to 57.71% conversion of EBITDA into free cash flow and 3.47% capital intensity, tempered by working-capital timing and receipts that may not repeat. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding leverage near the current range through the fourth-quarter taxes, on the Acute Care proceeds, and on market access at roughly the 5.875% coupon paid in June 2026 as the 2028 notes approach in 2027, with no agency rating to anchor that access. The primary downside path is Interventional weakness and fading one-offs while the revolver funds taxes and repurchases, lifting leverage against covenants that cannot be checked. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector the profile is stronger on margin and free of a sponsor, and weaker on stated policy; the filings give no peer data, so that comparison is a judgement. The financial profile trend is better on leverage and cash flow but is not comparable across periods because the perimeter changed. Further analysis would require the covenant compliance calculation, letters of credit, the OEM tax amount, the proxy statement, the executed agreements, a leverage target and the securitization and Term A-1 terms.
Analysis complete. Top risk: shareholder returns and tax payments absorbing the proceeds that reduced leverage.
